doc.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01

title: Joining the Southern Syncopators in Lake Charles
summary: Paul goes to Lake Charles in 1932 to join a band, adds a missed Oliver bandmate (Clarence Black), and lists the band's players.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Well anyway, in 1932 I was around New Orleans. I wasn't doing anything much around there. So I met my cousin, who's Baptiste. He said, my son Alex Ruschon is out in Lake Charles. He said, they got a good band out there. He said, why don't you go out there with them? Because Alexis had asked for me. He was a saxophone. He was my scholar and he was a good saxophone player. So I told him, I think I will. I'd go on out there. So I goes on out to Lake Charles. And I joins with that band. And they call it the Syncopators. They called it. That was the name of the band. Well we had a big fellow that was the leader. Oh by the way, I forgot to mention one more man in King Oliver's band. I hate to leave him out. Clarence Black.
He was a violin player. He was a violin in 1927 when we went to New York. I forgot to mention him.

Yeah, to St. Louis from New York. But anyway, I finished telling you. They called this band the Southern Syncopators. And they had Alan Prairie, the big 330 pound man. He was, all he did was directing. He looked good in front of the band. And we had D.D. on trumpet. D.D. Pierce?
He would sing A La Ba. D.D. Yeah.
And we had. Well by the way, who do you think wrote that? Where was the first time you ever heard that?
